page: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores using an x86_64 architecture. The underlying hardware is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache. The server is configured with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 7559 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No public IPv4 addresses are included by default, and there are no GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 109,987.08 and a Passmark CPU score of 103,274.51, placing it in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 8369.01 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 501.02 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), contribute to top-tier performance in extended instructions, encryption, and physics simulations. In database operations, the server achieved 33,828.73 operations on Passmark and 146.84 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. For LLM inference, prompt processing is highly efficient, reaching 303.22 tokens/sec on 7B models and 42.56 tokens/sec on 70B models, though text generation speeds are comparatively lower.

Given its high compute density and large local NVMe storage paired with a relatively low memory footprint, the D128lds_v6 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive RAM-to-CPU ratios. The massive 7559 GB local NVMe SSD provides high-speed local scratch space, making it highly suitable for large-scale software compilation, static web serving, high-throughput database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. It is also well-suited for CPU-based machine learning inference and cryptographic workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v6 is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs (64 physical cores), 256.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), and a bundled 7559 GB NVMe SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and strong cryptographic execution. Benchmark results highlight exceptional throughput in static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression, alongside robust CPU-based LLM prompt processing. With its low memory-to-CPU ratio and high-capacity local storage, the D128lds_v6 provides a cost-efficient hardware profile for compute-intensive workloads, software compilation, high-throughput databases, and web serving.
